subject: geography
title: KS3 Geography - Rivers
subtitle: Revision pack for river systems, processes, landforms, flooding, management and fieldwork.
description: A KS3 geography revision pack on how rivers work from source to mouth. It covers drainage basins, downstream change, river processes, landforms, flooding, flood management, case studies and fieldwork data skills.

data.title: Formation of a V-shaped valley
data.instruction: Put the stages of V-shaped valley formation in the correct order.
items: The river flows over a steep gradient in the upper course.
Vertical erosion cuts down into the river bed.
Weathering weakens rocks on the valley sides.
Loose material moves downslope under gravity.
The river carries the loosened material away.
A narrow, steep-sided V-shaped valley forms over time.

data.title: Formation of a waterfall and gorge
data.instruction: Put the waterfall formation stages in the correct order.
items: The river flows over bands of hard rock and soft rock.
Soft rock erodes more quickly by hydraulic action and abrasion.
A step, plunge pool and hard rock overhang form.
The unsupported hard rock overhang collapses.
Collapsed rocks help deepen the plunge pool by abrasion.
The waterfall retreats upstream and leaves a steep-sided gorge.

data.title: Formation of an oxbow lake
data.instruction: Put the oxbow lake formation stages in the correct order.
items: A river flows around a meander bend.
Erosion on the outside bends makes the meander wider.
Deposition happens on the inside bends where the flow is slower.
The neck of land between two bends becomes narrower.
During high flow, the river cuts through the narrow neck.
Deposition seals off the old bend, leaving an oxbow lake.

data.title: Fieldwork method for downstream change
data.instruction: Put the fieldwork stages in a sensible order.
items: Choose several safe sites at different distances downstream.
Measure width, depth, velocity and sediment size using the same method at each site.
Repeat measurements to improve reliability.
Record recent weather and site conditions.
Calculate averages where needed.
Describe patterns downstream using figures from the data.
